correctness.rationale: After k edge deletions the cycle consists of k paths. The expected count of vertices in size>=h open clusters on a path of length ell is F_h(ell)=0 if ell<h, else p^(h-1)[h+(ell-h)(h-(h-1)p)]. This follows by counting all-open h-windows and qualifying maximal-cluster starts. Merging two long paths lowers tail risk by (h-1)p^h; shifting vertices from the lone long path to short paths of length<h-1 strictly improves it. Hence zero-risk classification for n<=k(h-1) and unique positive-risk multiset {n-(k-1)(h-1),(h-1)^(k-1)}. Six-vertex p=3/4 maximum crossover follows from three exact length partitions, and n<=5 obstruction and h=2 identity rule out smaller transitions. Mean-cluster convexity gives balanced unique mean minimizer. Independently enumerated open-bond states for n=6,k=2,h=3 at p=1/2,3/4,4/5.
